definitions.explanation: Describes being completely exhausted, having no energy left.

examples.japanese: へとへとで{動|うご}けない。
examples.english: I'm so tired I can't move.

examples.japanese: {一日|いちにち}{中|じゅう}{働|はたら}いてへとへとになった。
examples.english: I worked all day and got exhausted.

notes:
へとへと is a mimetic word (オノマトペ) describing extreme physical exhaustion — being completely drained of energy.

GRAMMAR:
Functions as both a na-adjective and adverb.
- Predicate: へとへとだ/です (I'm exhausted)
- Adverbial: へとへとに{疲|つか}れる (to get dead tired)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- へとへとになる: to become exhausted
- へとへとに{疲|つか}れる: to get dead tired
- へとへとで〜できない: too tired to do ~
- もうへとへとだ: I'm completely wiped out

SIMILAR WORDS:
- くたくた: worn out (similar level, slightly less dramatic)
- ぐったり: limp, collapsed (emphasizes physical collapse)
- ばてる: to be worn out (verb form)
- {疲|つか}れた: tired (general — へとへと is much stronger)

REGISTER:
Casual and conversational. Not used in formal writing.
